The consulting leg generates $2700-$5850 per engagement while the SaaS leg plants a recurring revenue seed that grows independently. Both legs draw from the same warm network, and neither requires more than 15-20 hours per week to initiate.
top_3_for_human_review.why_this_person: Two existing users of the tool are embedded in the professional network. That is an extraordinary asset that most freelancers never have at week 1. The hybrid structure matches the stated preference for freelance income with few high-value clients while beginning the transition toward scalable product revenue. It fits under 30 hrs/week, no travel, no on-call, and starts paying within days.

recommendation.rationale: hybrid_002 is the only opportunity that turns an existing asset — two live warm-network users of a tool already built — into immediate dual-stream revenue without spending a single hour on cold outreach or product development. Every other opportunity requires either building something new, reaching people who don't already know the person, or waiting months for compounding to work. This opportunity starts with the rarest resource in freelance business development: people who have already experienced the value and trust the person delivering it. The consulting leg provides financial weight while the SaaS leg begins compounding. It fits every constraint, and the first action requires nothing more than sending two messages today.

Same network, clearly scoped offer, $2700-$5400 per engagement. Pursue this in parallel as the second outreach message in week 1 — it costs nothing to run both simultaneously.

scoring_notes: STANDARD weights applied. Content-only opportunities scored severely penalized on speed-to-first-dollar (4-6 month ramp incompatible with 8-week runway). SaaS opportunities penalized on speed and defensibility given build time and crowded markets. No automatic disqualifiers triggered. All deal-breakers checked: no opportunity requires travel or on-call support. Hybrid opportunities evaluated holistically for the 30 hr/week constraint.
